title: Structural Properties: Parity, Divisibility, and the Product Formula

problemStatement.formal: \varphi(n) \text{ is even for } n \geq 3; \quad \varphi(n) = n-1 \Leftrightarrow n \text{ prime}; \quad a \mid b \Rightarrow \varphi(a) \mid \varphi(b); \quad \varphi(a)\varphi(b) \leq \varphi(ab); \quad \varphi(n) = n\prod_{p|n}(1-1/p); \quad \varphi(\gcd(a,b))\varphi(ab) = \varphi(a)\varphi(b)\gcd(a,b)
problemStatement.plain: Structural properties of Euler totient function: parity (even for n>=3), prime characterization (phi(n)=n-1 iff prime), divisibility monotonicity, super-multiplicativity, the product formula, and the GCD-totient identity.
whyMatters: Foundational properties connecting totient to primality, divisibility, and factorization
Product formula underpins sieve methods and average-order estimates
GCD identity unifies multiplicativity and divisibility into one formula
